Welcome to Forres Sandle Manor
The New Forest's Leading Independent School for Pupils Ages 2-16
A warm welcome
Message from the Head
Welcome to Forres Sandle Manor, a vibrant day and boarding school for boys and girls aged 2-16, set in an idyllic 35-acre campus on the outskirts of the river town of Fordingbridge, in the heart of the New Forest.
With an average class size of less than 15 across the whole school, everyone at Forres Sandle Manor is well known and nobody is left out. Our school is full of kind, caring and hard-working pupils and inspirational teachers who help to instil a love of learning in all that they do.
For boys and girls ages 2 to 16
Life at Forres Sandle Manor
Set in 35 acres of beautiful grounds on the edge of the New Forest, our School’s location is recorded as far back as the Doomsday Book. Today, we provide a holistic, rounded education that prepares children for the next stage of their education and for adult life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wellbeing & Pastoral Care – Forres Sandle Manor
pageCache.text:
Wellbeing & Pastoral Care
At FSM, the wellbeing of every child is our priority, and we take the responsibility of their care very seriously. We understand that every pupil is unique, with individual pastoral needs.
We are committed to encouraging a nurturing environment where every child feels secure, supported, and engaged. Our ultimate aim is to provide a physical, emotional, and intellectual space where each pupil can thrive and achieve happiness and success.
This nurturing approach is supported by strong relationships between tutors, subject teachers, boarding staff, and parents. The Tutor System plays a vital role in bridging the gap between home and school, with Class Teachers and Form Tutors serving as the primary point of contact. Additionally, our dedicated Pastoral Care Team is always available to provide further support when needed.
At FSM, we are fortunate to have a dedicated team ready to support pupils with their wellbeing, emotions, or challenges they may face. In addition to Form Tutors, our Key Stage Coordinators provide an extra layer of care, offering guidance and running tailored interventions when needed.
We are also developing our ELSA (Emotional Literacy Support Assistant) provision and offer a weekly Listening Ear Service, which can be arranged through Mrs. Marks, our Deputy Head Pastoral, for additional external support.
As part of our commitment to comprehensive care for pupils and their families, we have partnered with Endsleigh Insurance to provide tailored insurance solutions and wellbeing resources for the education sector. With nearly 60 years of experience and a reputation for working with leading schools across the UK, Endsleigh ensures parents have easy access to secure, flexible cover and expert guidance whenever needed.
We believe it’s vital to talk and equally important to find the right person to talk to. With a wide range of skills and resources available in-house, as well as strong links to external support services, FSM is well-equipped to provide the care and assistance every child needs.
Mentoring
Each child in the Prep School is paired with a Senior Mentor. This initiative supports our through-school ethos by giving younger pupils someone they can talk to and rely on. Senior students, in turn, develop valuable leadership and communication skills as they support their mentees.
School Council
Our School Council meets weekly, with one of its key focus areas being pupil wellbeing. The Council has been allocated a budget and is currently designing a wellbeing space that will be accessible to everyone in the school. Watch this space for updates!
Wellbeing Check-ins
Every week, tutors dedicate time during tutor sessions for a ‘wellbeing window.’ During this time, pupils can record how they’re feeling in their journals. This approach is particularly helpful for those who find it difficult to express their emotions verbally. It also provides tutors with valuable insight into how their pupils are feeling and allows for timely support when needed.
FSM Troopers
Many of our boarders come from military families. To support these pupils, we run a group called FSM Troopers. This weekly meeting provides a safe and supportive space for children whose parents are on deployment. The group allows pupils to share their feelings, learn from each other—especially with older children guiding younger ones—and explore practical ways to navigate the weeks and months ahead.
Assemblies
Every Monday, we hold an assembly for our Prep and Senior pupils. The assembly introduces a theme that becomes the focus for tutors throughout the week. Our Prep pupils attend an additional assembly on Wednesday to reinforce this theme. Many of these themes are designed to foster values and skills that support wellbeing, such as building resilience, promoting kindness, understanding anti-bullying practices, and exploring positive role models.
Our Learning Centre
At FSM, we recognise that everyone learns differently, and our Learning Centre is here to support pupils with specific learning needs. For children with learning difficulties, school life can present unique challenges. That’s why our approach is embraced by the entire school community.
We believe teaching should be active, engaging, and multi-sensory because good teaching for dyslexic pupils is good teaching for all pupils. We are committed to ensuring all children feel challenged yet successful and are encouraged to set realistic goals for themselves.
Our pupils with identified learning differences often excel as creative thinkers, talented athletes, gifted musicians, capable artists, and clever problem-solvers. The Learning Centre staff work closely with class teachers to ensure every child’s needs are met, both individually and within the broader classroom environment.
Life Skills Programme
All pupils participate in a weekly Life Skills lesson as part of our PSHE programme, guided by the Jigsaw curriculum. These sessions provide opportunities to explore and discuss important topics, with regular checkpoints focusing on wellbeing. Themes include Celebrating Differences, Being Me in My World, Healthy Me, and Relationships, encouraging self-awareness, empathy, and resilience.

Weekend Provision
The curriculum at Forres Sandle Manor runs from Monday to Friday, but in addition to ensuring our boarding pupils are actively engaged at weekends, we also believe it is important to offer our local pupils the opportunity to further extend their learning and personal development should they wish.
Every Sunday, during term time, we take all of our boarding pupils on a day trip to a local place of interest, or one further afield. The list of trips will be published prior to the start of each term and it is our ambition that day pupils will be able to opt-in to these trips on a case-by-case basis, thereby enabling them to enjoy more time with their friends, visiting places of particular interest.
Find out more about our boarding here.
Every Saturday morning during term time, all FSM pupils from Years 3 and above are welcome to participate in our Super-Curriculum sessions. There are two sessions, each lasting 90 minutes (with a break in between), which means that pupils wishing to participate will be in school from 9 am until 12:30 pm. Every half term, our aim is to provide pupils with an ever-expanding range of sessions which will enable them to find new passions and interests.
Sessions are run both on and off-site, with the latter usually spanning across both sessions to enable the pupils to travel to and from a venue and have over 2 hours to enjoy an activity.

Academic
At Forres Sandle Manor, whatever your child’s starting point, they will receive an outstanding academic experience.
Developing individual academic excellence in every pupil means ensuring we honour three commitments:
1. Outstanding teachers
– We are a forward-looking school, but one traditional value remains important to us – passionate, engaging and highly effective teaching. We pride ourselves on having the area’s most inspiring teaching staff who seek to instil a love of their subject(s) into every lesson.
2. Small classes
– Whether it is being stretched and challenged, or at other times being supported and encouraged, we expect every teacher to interact with every pupil on a 1-1 basis in every lesson. That means we cap classes at 20 but aim to have classes averaging 12-15 pupils.
3. A personalised curriculum
– We have designed our curriculum to fit the ethos of our school. As they enter our Senior School, that means providing all of them with a huge breadth of study by studying over 12 subjects, using every specialist space we have across our wonderful 35-acre campus.
From the start of Year 9, having experienced two years’ breadth, it is time for them to specialise by choosing the ‘optional’ subjects they wish to continue with. This selection is further refined at the start of Year 10 when they commence their GCSE courses. In this way, we achieve the balance of broadening young minds, then empowering them to make informed choices in the curriculum areas best suited to their strengths and interests.
Individual Academic Excellence – Years 9-11
In addition to a continuing focus on outstanding progress in English, Mathematics and Science, from the start of Year 9, we enable our pupils to choose 6 ‘optional’ subjects to continue with. This gives our pupils several advantages:
1.Most importantly, they are able to select the subjects where their passions and talents are best suited, thereby making their school days even more enjoyable as they prepare for GCSEs.
2.By removing some subjects, more time can be allocated to chosen subjects, enabling greater progress to be made.
3.This process of selection, also ensures that our average class sizes are reduced even further from Year 9, ensuring even more support and challenge from our fantastic teachers at a crucial time for our pupils.
At the start of Year 10, this choice of 6 subjects is further refined down to 4, which will complete their GCSE subject selection(s). This ensures that the vast majority of our pupils will sit ten GCSES:
-Plus 4 subjects of their choosing.
Throughout their time in Years 9-11, pupils continue to have weekly Sports/Games lessons (including time for fixtures) and Life Skills lessons.
To find more and apply for scholarships click here.
A Strong Core
Every pupil, at Forres Sandle Manor, makes outstanding progress in English, Mathematics and Science and in designing our curriculum, these disciplines are at the centre of our planning.
Pupils in these year groups have 4 lessons per week in both English and Mathematics, ensuring these appear almost every day on their timetables.
In Science, we go even further by splitting Science into specialist Biology, Chemistry and Physics lessons right from the start of Year 7. This is in preparation for Years 9-11 when all pupils are entered for Triple Science (enabling them to achieve a separate GCSE qualification in each). We ensure our science lessons are as practical and ‘hands on’ as possible.
An outstanding sports and games provision continues to be part of our curriculum, including time each week for fixtures.
Breadth of Study
In addition to the above, we also want our pupils to experience the broadest possible curriculum, with each subject taught by a specialist in a dedicated teaching space. Our outstanding campus enables every pupil to enjoy working practically in dedicated and purpose-built teaching spaces, ensuring lessons are as engaging and inspiring as possible.
It is our ambition that all pupils will study:
Dance, Drama, Music, Art, Food Studies, Design Technology, Computing/ICT, History, Geography, French/Spanish and Life Skills.
This breadth of study enables all our pupils to broaden their minds, creating new opportunities for each of them to thrive.

Enrichment Programme
At Forres Sandle Manor, our Enrichment Programme is designed to be a fundamental part of helping pupils to be happy and successful, and contributes to their outstanding personal development. We believe that pupils need to have dedicated time at the start of each day to learn something new, experience something that further readies them for life beyond education. This is why we created our Enrichment Programme.
To achieve this, all of our Senior School pupils begin their day with lesson one as an Extended Curriculum (‘Enrichment’) session. Every term, all Senior School pupils can choose from a huge range of sessions (1 per day), which often bring pupils with similar passions together from different year groups.
Find out about our co-curricular programme here.
For our pupils, the Enrichment Programme has several benefits:
1. It provides them with a chance to start every day (when teenagers are often least likely to learn effectively in a classroom setting), with an activity they have chosen. A great way to start every day at school!
2. Socially, it enables them to spend time and make friends with peers from different year groups who enjoy the same interests.
3. For older pupils, it provides meaningful opportunities to develop and show leadership. For those in the younger years, seeing older role models gives them something to aspire to.
4. Every pupil can enjoy weekly sessions for at least a term, enabling each to have a purposeful outcome, for example, a performance or additional qualification.

House System
Every great school needs a thriving house system and our 4 houses are:
Broomy, Hasley, Pittswood & Sloden.
Across the school, each pupil and nearly every member of staff is a member of a House. Siblings are always in the same House.
The House System & Senior School
As a Senior School pupil, there are unique opportunities to participate in and become a leader within our House system.
Firstly, all pupils are able to compete in competitions across the year. Our ambition for the House system is to ensure that every pupil in the school can find events that they genuinely want to participate in and where they feel they can excel.
By participating in these events, pupils can win points for their House but also compete alongside friends in their year group, as well as pupils from across other year groups in the school.
Most importantly, as a Senior School pupil, there is the chance to apply for various House student leadership positions. House Captain and House Vice Captain roles will be introduced for Senior School pupils. Those appointed will play a significant part in the life of the whole school, including supporting the other pupils who hold House leadership positions.

Trips and Excursions
At Forres Sandle Manor, trips and excursions are seen as an integral part of the school experience as they enable our pupils to explore, enrich and elevate their learning and social skills.
From Year 7, all the way through to Year 11, our pupils have the opportunity to enjoy taking their learning out of the classroom and into the world.
Based within the UK and overseas, these trips contribute to ensuring the Senior School experience at Forres Sandle Manor is exceptional.
Senior School Trips
Ski Trip to Passo Tonale in Italy. This is a bi-annual week-long residential, usually during the Easter holidays, open to all pupils from Year 5 and above.
All abilities are welcome, including those who would like to try skiing for the first time.
Sports Tours
We hold both UK and European Sports Tours that run alternate years. These are an opportunity to present all our children’s hard work on the national and international stage. All of these trips run within our Half Term or Easter holidays.
Arctic Adventure
One of the highlights for Seniors is the opportunity to experience an Arctic adventure! Staying in a cabin near the Arctic Circle, they enjoy activities, such as skiing, snow-shoeing, dog sledding, ice fishing, and fat biking. From this, they gain an understanding of traditional life and the environment.
UK and International Expeditions
We are excited to offer our Seniors, both UK and international educational expeditions, from the Brecons to the Azores. Pupils have the chance to enjoy the outdoors, learning skills, such as map reading, outdoor cookery and resilience. They are able to challenge themselves, gaining an appreciation of the natural world, whilst developing new skills.
Find out more about Boarding at Forres Sandle Manor here.
Residential Week
Our residential week for pupils is always a highlight of the school year and takes place in June. Our Year 7 and 8 students have an amazing experience in either beautiful Normandy or Cornwall (alternating years between the two destinations). Our pupils have a wonderful time exploring the unique cultures, landscapes, and activities that these regions have to offer.
Our Year 9 and 10 pupils have an exciting opportunity to experience two trips to continental Europe. During their visits, they explore iconic landmarks and local communities, allowing them to gain a deeper appreciation of European culture.

After-School Activities

Armed Forces Families
Forres Sandle Manor has a long and proud association with military families.
We offer a very supportive environment for serving families. House parents and Matrons are experienced in supporting military children throughout their time at the School. Help is given to boarders to keep in touch with loved ones wherever they might be in the world, provide a listening ear, advice and support and are always on hand round-the-clock…and even a hug when it is needed!
Supporting Armed Forces (FSM Troopers) Group
A good number of our boarders are from military families, so we run a Supporting Active Service group ‘FSM Troopers’ which provides additional support for children when a parent is away on deployment. The weekly meetings allow children in similar situations to share their feelings, learn from each other (especially the older children assisting the younger), and explore practical ways to help in the weeks and months ahead.
Boarding at Forres Sandle Manor
Find out more about Boarding at Forres Sandle Manor here
Fees for Military Families
We are able to accept the CEA and offer a CEA+10%* fee structure. Please contact our Admissions team here for more information about our fees for military families.

Armed Forces Covenant
Forres Sandle Manor has enjoyed a longstanding relationship with members of the Armed Forces and their families. As such, we are a registered member of the Armed Forces Covenant. We pledge to support Remembrance Day, Armed Forces Day, the Poppy Appeal and support our military children with our Support Armed Services (SAS) group, amongst a number of other items.

Friends of Sandle Manor – FOSM
Friends of Sandle Manor (FOSM) is a voluntary social and fundraising committee made up of parents and staff. The Committee aims to foster social links within the School and to enhance the school experience for a broad cross-section of children.
As well as organising social events, the Committee is responsible for identifying, funding and delivering projects for the benefit of the school community outside the scope of the Educational Trust.
Traditionally, FOSM has organised, or contributed to, events throughout the school year. These normally follow a pattern but with different themes. In recent years, these have been:
Events Autumn Term
FOSM Mad Hatter’s Tea Party
Our Mad Hatter’s Tea Party is a particular favourite. From whimsical hats to a delightful tea, the event held in our Dudley Hill Hall is always a magical afternoon filled with fun and laughter.
Events Spring Term
The DHH becomes the ‘Dudley Hill Arms’ for the evening and teams of 8 – 10 compete for a range of prizes. The quality of the team names may raise a groan but the standard and breadth of knowledge is always high. This is a very friendly and informal evening which normally includes both the FOSM bar and outside catering.
Pre Prep Coffee Morning
Many of the FOSM social events take place in the evening, which may be difficult for Lower School parents and so each year the FOSM Committee makes a special effort to include the parents of the younger pupils. The Easter Bunny is given extra support by FOSM during the Pre Prep Easter Egg hunt, after which FOSM hosts a coffee morning for the parents.
Events Summer term
Our FOSM Summer Fête, held in early May, is a wonderful event set in the Manor grounds, with food, drink and lots of family entertainment including stalls run by our Prep School pupils.
FOSM is proud to contribute to the atmosphere of celebration by providing some outside support in the form of food and drink. In the past this has included a coffee stand, Bubbly Bar (serving cold drinks and Prosecco) and a hog roast. International Admissions
Forres Sandle Manor welcome students from all countries and backgrounds. The application process is slightly longer for an international child, but we are here to make it as simple as possible for you.
Book in a Phone Call or Skype Chat
We’re aware that you’re unlikely to be able to make a visit to the School. We like to talk to parents and children as part of the application process. We can book a telephone conversation or Skype chat at your convenience. This way you can ask any questions you may have. We can get the relevant staff to be available, including the Headmaster. Just email Admissions to arrange this.
Making an Application
Should you choose for your child to come to Forres Sandle Manor, please email admissions@fsmschool.com with your country of origin, and we will send the relevant paperwork to begin an application.
We will guide you through each step of the way – from application to the first few weeks of a pupil being with us.

Pre Prep
Pre Prep – Nursery to Year 2
True education begins long before exams are even on the horizon: the way we are taught in our early years has a huge influence on our long-term love of learning and the person we will eventually become.
Instead of hot-housing, we give children the most precious thing of all – time. It’s only by having time to explore new concepts that a child is able to ask the questions that might not have occurred to anyone else, to make connections to their past experiences, and to become fully immersed in a subject.
Our creative early years curriculum sees classes choosing an exciting new topic every term or half term, with everything they learn during that time linking to the theme as much as possible. This makes learning far more meaningful for the children and, because they are involved in investigating the topic and have a say in what they will study, they become active rather than passive learners.
Pre Prep Outdoor Learning
Some of the most valuable learning in these early years happens outside the classroom, and we aim to provide as many opportunities as we can for children to explore the world. With this in mind, each class goes on a fact-finding mission when a new topic is introduced: for example, our reception class recently visited the Historic Dockyards in Portsmouth to kick off their ‘Pirates, Parrots and Pieces of Eight’ topic.
Pre Prep Activities
We have a vast and varied selection of Pre Prep activities. You can find out more here.
Teaching in the Pre Prep is predominantly by class teachers except for PE, art, music, ICT and languages, which are taught by specialists. There is no formal homework – just regular reading, spelling and times tables to learn – and although we assess children regularly, there are no formal exams. Our aim in Pre Prep is to create a lively and vibrant environment which promotes an independence of spirit, a willingness to ‘have a go,’ and a determination to succeed.
